newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-FACT FILE FOR REAL MADRID-REAL BETIS GAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FACT FILE FOR REAL MADRID-REAL BETIS GAME.

text.p: Facts and figures for the Real Madrid-Real Betis Spanish championship match to be played at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium on Saturday (kick-off 1930 GMT):
Real Madrid: Founded in 1902.
Major honours: League champions (record 26 times): 1932,
1987, 1988, 1989, 1990, 1995. Spanish Cup winners (17 times):
1985, 1986. Inter Continental Cup 1960.
Ground: Santiago Bernabeu stadium (named after club president
in glory days of 1950s and 60s), capacity 106,000.
Manager: Fabio Capello (Italy).
Record appearances: Carlos Santillana, 461.
Real Betis: Founded 1907.
Major honours: League champions 1934-35. Spanish Cup 1977.
Ground: Benito Villamarin stadium (named after a former club
president), capacity 47,000.
Manager: Lorenzo Serra Ferrer
Record Appearances: Julio Cardenosa 306
Games between Real Madrid and Betis:
Real Madrid at home - played 34, won 21, drawn 10, lost 3.
Betis at home - played 35, won 13, drawn 10, lost 12.
Total (Real Madrid first): played 69, won 33, drawn 20, lost
Other facts:

--Real Madrid's reserve team plays -- alongside the reserves of Atletico Madrid and Barcelona -- in the Spanish second division. Their third team plays in one of the four groups of the third, or second B division, alongside the Betis second team.
--Real Madrid are known as 'el Madrid' ('the Madrid') or 'el Real', Real Betis is usually shortened to 'Betis'.

--The prefix 'Real' which means 'royal' is also held by many other clubs, although in some cases it is rarely used. Zaragoza, Sporting Gijon, Espanyol, Deportivo Coruna, Valladolid, Racing Santander, Celta Vigo, Oviedo and Real Sociedad are the 10 other clubs in first division which also hold been granted the title of 'royal'.
--Both club shields incorporate a shield to reflect their royal patronage.

--Betis were the first winners of the Spanish Cup when it became known as the 'Copa del Rey' ('the King's Cup') in 1977. It had previously been known as the 'Copa del Generalisimo' after the late dictator, General Franco.

--King Juan Carlos of Spain remains discreetly above allegiance to a club because of the highly-politicised nature of regional loyalty in the country. But his mother, Dona Mercedes, is an ardent Betis fan who was guest of honour at a game last season.

--Someone believed to be a closet 'Betico' (Betis fan) is former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez, who was born not far from the Villamarin stadium but has diplomatically refused to reveal his loyalties.

--The name Betis was given by the Romans to the river that flows through the southern city of Seville. By extension the big southern region (now called Andalucia) was called 'Baetica'. The river is now called 'Guadalquivir', from the Arabic meaning 'big river', but there is still a riverside street called 'Betis'.

--Because of the Roman name of their club a group of flamboyant Betis fans founded a supporters club called 'Augustus' before an away match in another Roman city, Merida. Members of the club, which still exists, wore Roman togas for the game.

--The Betis slogan is 'Viva er Beti manque pierda' ('Long live Betis, even in defeat') which is written to reflect the idiosyncracies of Andalucian pronunciation -- final 's' sounds are often missed, making 'Betis' into 'Beti'.
--Real Madrid play in an all-white strip and their fans are sometimes called 'merengues' (meringues) as a result.

--Real Madrid's reserves, until recently known as 'Castilla' after the Spanish heartland, play in the 'Ciudad Deportiva' (sports city), a centrally located training complex, part of which is to be sold off to pay the club's debts, which are estimated at 12 billion pesetas (around $95 million).
--Real were founding members of the Spanish first division in 1928-29. They share with Athletic Bilbao and Barcelona the distinction of never having been relegated.
--Betis, by contrast, have spent 34 years in the first divison, 24 in the second and seven in the third.
--Real Madrid's basketball side has been just as successful in the European Cup as the football outfit but the club no longer has other sports teams associated with it.

--An annual Oxford-Cambridge rowing regatta between supporters of Betis and arch-rivals Sevilla has been running for over 30 years. There are fewer quality oarsmen among the less affluent Betis supporters and as a result Sevilla have a far better record.

Betis owner Manuel Ruiz de Lopera became so unhappy at the repeated defeats that he disowned the regatta and threatened to take legal action against those using the Betis name. Despite this the race took place again this January, with Betis winning on a disqualification.

--Although few people would dispute that Argentine striker Alfredo di Stefano was Real Madrid's greatest-ever player, he may not be the most famous. Latin singing idol Julio Iglesias was once a goalkeeper for one of the club's reserve teams and took up music only because of an injury.

--Betis's most famous player was international winger Rafael Gordillo, who signed for Real Madrid in 1985 before returning to Betis in 1991. His testimonial game was played against Real Madrid in 1995.
